The slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=0$ equals the function's derivative at the corresponding point.

We have the function 

$$
y={(\sqrt{2x+1})}^{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(\sqrt{2x+1})}^{{x}^{2}+1}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =({x}^{2}+1)\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(({x}^{2}+1)\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2x+1})) \\ \frac{1}{y}\,{y}^{′} & =({x}^{2}+1)^{′}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2x+1})+({x}^{2}+1)\,{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2x+1}))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\,{y}^{′} & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{2x+1})+({x}^{2}+1)\,(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+1}}\cdot \frac{2}{2\sqrt{2x+1}}) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)+\frac{{x}^{2}+1}{2x+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y\,(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)+\frac{{x}^{2}+1}{2x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y={(\sqrt{2x+1})}^{{x}^{2}+1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={(\sqrt{2x+1})}^{{x}^{2}+1}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)+\frac{{x}^{2}+1}{2x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of $y={(\sqrt{2x+1})}^{{x}^{2}+1}$ at $x=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={y}^{′}{|}_{x=0} & ={(\sqrt{2(0)+1})}^{(0)^{2}+1}(0\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(2(0)+1)+\frac{(0)^{2}+1}{2(0)+1}) \\  & =1\cdot (0\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+1) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
